# A reachable bond-distance matching that ends at the next round

**Standard statement.** A permutation can preserve every pair's least common bond size in a graph generated by the complete-round parity law, fix every live vertex star pointwise, and still have no extension to the next graph's table. Two edges already internal to the graph witness failure. The graph has ten ordinary vertices and is obtained in one round from a connected start with six. The same obstruction holds when loose distinctions at a live junction may be re-paired.

**Nearest known result.** In the earlier tested populations, all 1,746,752 qualifying census self-symmetries and 36,060 qualifying matchings of carried pairs extended. The static seven-junction example lacked a positive-age history. The six-junction start below has repeated meetings. The admissible starts of the small census had at most five junctions, and the larger carried-pair study required junctions to meet at most once. [Earlier range](../../../research/HUNT-SHORTEN-20261119-001/hunt_shorten.md) · [Meaning of the growing end](../../../research/EXTEND-ROUND-20261119-001/extend_round.md)

## A start and two forced rounds

Use the even parity equation on each row. A distinction in only one row is loose. For reading bond distances one may join every loose distinction to the common outside vertex. In that graph a bond is the cut between two connected shores. Equivalently it is a support-minimal nonzero equation. The bond distance of a pair is one less than the size of the smallest bond containing it.

| Starting junction | Its distinctions |
| --- | --- |
| M | 0, 1, 2, 3 |
| A | 0, 1, 4, 5 |
| B | 2, 3, 13, 14 |
| S | 4, 6, 9, 10 |
| D | 5, 6, 7, 8, 11 |
| E | 7, 8, 12 |

The start is connected. Every distinction has one or two holders. Each listed support is itself a bond. The same is true for every junction of the next two stages, by enumeration of all bonds. In particular, projected onto any one of these supports, the allowed states obey just its displayed parity equation. It passes the finite K1–K3 test.

In round one the candidate pairs of live sites are S,D (common neighbor A) and S,E (common neighbor D). D and E lack a common neighbor, and B has none in common with another live site. The two leftover distinctions at B give two offshoots. Denote the four resulting sites by X, Y, U, V. In round two the candidate pairs are X,Y (through S) and U,V (through B). U and V each have one leftover for an offshoot.

| Round | New supports, in order | New distinctions per support |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | X = {9,11,15}, Y = {10,12,16}, U = {13,17,18}, V = {14,19,20} | 1, 1, 2, 2 |
| 2 | J = {15,16,21}, K = {17,19,22,23}, L = {18,24,25}, N = {20,26,27} | 1, 2, 2, 2 |

For the cheapest count at a site with p parents, the three bounds here are one fresh distinction, at least 3−p for its arity, and the number of groups that need the site in the lookahead round. No proposed site takes all old loose distinctions, so the implied-equation exception does not occur. The lookahead demands are (1,1,1,1) in the first round and (0,2,1,1) in the second. In the latter, K shares one parent with L and another with N. L and N have no common parent. These counts give the displayed supports. The choices of numbers for fresh distinctions and the order within a holder are arbitrary names. The ten-junction stage also lies outside the old at-most-five-start census at every later age. Removing its four live sites recovers the six displayed starting junctions. Those cannot themselves be a positive-age stage because S and D are live and meet. The unique-predecessor theorem would force any history of length at least two to pass through that impossible stage. ## Every current pair and the growing end

Consider the ten-junction stage after the first round. Let φ exchange 0 with 2 and fix all other distinctions. Site M has just the two bits 0,1 to A and the two bits 2,3 to B. All four are already shared. The four live supports X,Y,U,V contain none of them. The permutation fixes every live support pointwise, all six loose distinctions, and the families of live sites met by each common neighbor.

For a bond through a middle distinction and any name outside the four, the holders A and B must be on opposite shores. If they were on the same shore, the only connected opposite shore containing M would be the singleton M, whose boundary has just the four middle names. When A and B are on opposite shores, moving M to the opposite shore keeps both shores connected. M was attached solely to one ordinary neighbor on its former shore and reattaches to the other neighbor. The move exchanges the two size-two sets of middle crossings and leaves every other crossing alone. It is reversible. All four middle distinctions therefore have identical readings to any fixed distinction outside those four.

For a mixed pair, one name from each of {0,1} and {2,3}, every cut through it holds all four names. The singleton M gives a bond of size four, since deleting M leaves a connected graph. For a pair from the same side, a cut with A and B on opposite shores needs two more crossings after M is deleted. Indeed two A–B paths avoiding M have disjoint distinction sets. Their labels in order are (4,9,15,17,13) and (5,7,12,16,19,14). Each goes through the outside vertex. If A and B are on the same shore, all four middle names cross together. Thus every one of the six middle pairs has minimum bond size four and distance three. All 210 pair distances agree under φ.

## A single old entry prevents every extension

After round two, the shore {A,S,D,E,X,Y,J} has boundary exactly {0,1,21}. The shore is connected through A, S and D, and its complement is connected through M, B and the right-hand new sites to the outside. A two-distinction bond through 0,1 is impossible. Separating A from B requires at least one more crossing because A and B are still connected after deleting M. Placing A and B together would make all four middle names cross. Hence the new bond distance between 0 and 1 is **two**.

The image pair 2,1 still forces all four middle distinctions across every cut containing it. Deleting M still leaves a connected graph, so its singleton shore attains four. The new bond distance between 2 and 1 is **three**. No permutation on the fresh names can change either old entry. Re-pairing old loose names at their holders also leaves 0,1,2 untouched. This proves the counterexample against both extension conventions. ## Precisely what the round reveals

All 24 permutations of the four middle names fix the first table and the growing end. At the second stage the within-side pairs {0,1} and {2,3} both read two, and all four cross-side pairs read three. For {2,3}, move M across the two shores of the size-three bond above. Exactly eight permutations preserve the partition {{0,1},{2,3}}, and precisely these eight extend. Every such permutation is generated by swaps inside the two pairs and by exchange of both pairs. An exchange of both pairs adds the parity row of M to the respective rows of A and B. It preserves the equation span. All future new supports avoid the four old shared names, so the same eight work with the identity on fresh distinctions at every later complete round of this history.

One current three-distinction reading exposes the particular lost distinction. The shore {A,S,D,E,X,Y} has boundary {0,1,15,16}. The smallest bond holding 0,1,15 has size four by the pair bound. No bond holds 2,1,15 since a bond holding 2 and 1 is the singleton M cut. This separates the example before the round. The sufficiency of all three-distinction readings in general remains open.

This is a marked self-symmetry on a single reachable stage. Its identity still extends. The result refutes the assertion that *every* matching of the full pair table and the growing end extends. It leaves the existential question for two distinct stages, and the question restricted to starts in which junctions meet at most once, open. One round's parent groups and fresh counts are still determined by the growing end. Equation-span-preserving matching still has the previously proved extension. Global minimality of six starting junctions is untested.
